Observe: Equivalent only when source identity, payload meaning, time/context, provenance, and payload hash are the same after canonical serialization. Different source or observation time is not equivalent.
ValidateObservation: Evidence-reference ordering may be equivalent if the contract treats it as a set, but validator identity, validation code, observation target, and integrity result must be the same.
AdmitEvidence: Ordering of identical observation refs can be harmless; a different registry record, payload hash, or provenance chain is not equivalent.
RejectEvidence: Equivalent only with the same evidence target and materially same bounded rejection reason. A different reason code is transition-distinct because history must explain why evidence was rejected.
CreateClaim: Canonical wording may be equivalent if proposition semantics and scope are identical. In runtime, different immutable IDs remain history-distinct; identity-renamed synthetic worlds may be scored structurally equivalent.
CreateBelief: Only the same claim reference and same belief semantics are equivalent; belief creation is never equivalent to verification.
Support: Evidence-ref ordering may be harmless, but Support is never interchangeable with Contradict or Undercut.
Contradict: Evidence-ref ordering may be harmless. Contradiction requires opposition to proposition content and is not equivalent to an undercut of evidence reliability.
Undercut: Equivalent only when the same evidentiary/support link is defeated for the same bounded reason. Not equivalent to contradiction.
Merge: Input object ordering can be equivalent when merge strategy is commutative and output/provenance is identical. Different strategies or conflict handling are not equivalent.
Split: Partition ordering can be equivalent when partition membership and provenance are identical. Any lost source content makes it non-equivalent/unsafe.
NarrowScope: Different textual scope expressions are equivalent only if they canonicalize to the exact same narrower scope. A stricter but different scope is safe-alternative, not exact equivalent.
ExpandScope: Only exact same resultant scope and proof/authority context count as equivalent. Any broader or differently bounded expansion is materially different.
Verify: Equivalent only when target, verification semantics, required evidence, and proof obligations are materially identical. A different evidence subset can change assurance and must not automatically count as equivalent.
Invalidate: Equivalent only for the same target and materially same reason/evidence basis. Invalidate is not equivalent to Suspend.
Suspend: Equivalent only when the same target is placed into the same non-final suspended condition with same reason/evidence. It is not falsity or invalidation.
Expire: Equivalent only with the same target and trusted-time fact. Host-clock-only expiration is not equivalent.
Reevaluate: Trigger-evidence ordering may be equivalent if set semantics apply; changing the trigger or target is not.
Adjudicate: Equivalent only with the same authorized outcome and materially same evidence/decision basis. Different legal outcomes are not equivalent merely because both are VM-legal.
Authorize: No broad semantic equivalence. Subject, scope, operation, consequence, consumer, key, nonce/use limit, expiry, and source bindings must be exact.
RejectAuthorization: Equivalent only if it rejects the same requested authority for the same material reason and source basis; a request for more evidence vs permanent prohibition should remain distinct.
Execute: No practical semantic equivalence beyond canonical serialization of the exact same authorized consequence. Different physical/tool consequences are different actions.
Rollback: No practical semantic equivalence beyond canonical serialization of the exact same authorized compensating consequence. Different rollback targets or scopes are materially different.
